# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 76 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 76 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_076_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Part 3 — The Rejected Stones

**76:1** But some stones were brought from the deep and placed in the building, and they fit with the stones that were put in from the plain. For they were very bright. But some of these were brought by the men and did not fit into the building. These were set aside near the tower, for they could not be used in the building, since they had not received the seal. For the others had the seal of the virgins.

**76:2** "Who are these virgins?" I asked the shepherd. "They are holy spirits," he said. "And a man cannot enter the kingdom of God in any other way except that these clothe him. For if you receive only the name but do not receive the garment from them, it profits you nothing. For these virgins are the Powers of the Son of God. If you bear the name but do not bear his power, you will bear his name in vain."

**76:3** "But the stones," I said, "that were rejected — who are they?" "These," he said, "are those who bore the name but did not put on the garment of the virgins." "And what is their garment, lord?" I said. "The names themselves are the garment," he said. "Everyone who bears the name of the Son of God ought also to bear the names of these virgins. For even the Son of God himself bears the names of these virgins."

**76:4** "But the stones that were thrown far away from the tower and fell on the road and rolled off the road onto the rough places — who are they?" "These," he said, "are those who believed but then because of their double-mindedness abandoned their true road. Thinking that they could find a better road, they went astray and were tormented, walking in the rough places."

**76:5** "But those that fell into the fire and were burned — who are they?" "These," he said, "are those who completely apostasized from the living God and it no longer entered their minds to repent, on account of the desires of their licentiousness and the wicked deeds they committed."

**76:6** "And who are those that fell near the water and could not be rolled into the water?" "These," he said, "are those who heard the word and wished to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then when the purity of the truth came into their memory, they changed their minds and went back after their evil desires."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the rejected stone categories and the virgins-as-virtues teaching of Similitude 9.*
